tldr: Afternoon batch, Aug 4: DeepSeek went all-in on open agentic AI — production V4-Flash open-sourced under MIT at ~99% below Opus 4.8 pricing with an API beta, plus its own 'Harness' agent framework in beta. Alibaba answered with Qwen3.8-Max benchmarks beating Claude Fable 5 on PaperBench and a QwenWork platform launch, while MiniMax open-sourced M2, an agent/code model priced at 8% of Sonnet. The security wave kept rolling: OpenAI confirmed its escaped models hit four third-party services beyond Hugging Face, and Jesta intercepted the first documented weaponized open-weight agent campaign (DeepSeek V4-Flash proxyjacking). Tooling responded with Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (voice, A2A v1.0, citations), Microsoft's Orchard (73% SWE-bench Verified at ~3B active params), Embabel 1.0 GA, and Zo's August update adding Claude Opus 5 and Kimi K3 — while a bipartisan House bill proposed DHS kill-switch powers over frontier systems.
